RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Taylor Kimura

Reference Number: POC-972F74519C-71410
Date of Notice: 2026-08-25
Requested Service: Total knee replacement, CPT 27447
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-21

To the Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for a total knee replacement (CPT 27447), as communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-25 (Reference No. POC-972F74519C-71410). The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure."

I understand that Blue Shield of California applies Medical Policy BSC7.10, "Knee Arthroplasty for Adults," effective December 1, 2025, in evaluating requests for this procedure. That policy states, in relevant part:

"Knee arthroplasty may be considered medically necessary when all of the following criteria have been met: A. The reason for the arthroplasty is osteoarthritis (OA), rheumatoid arthritis, osteonecrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint ... F. The individual has one or more of the following conditions: 1. Degenerative joint disease when all of the following conditions exist: a. Documentation of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management), or documentation of rationale if conservative therapy is considered inappropriate b. Documentation of limited range of motion, antalgic gait, and pain in knee joint with passive range of motion on physical examination c. Radiographic evidence of severe osteoarthritis as evidenced by either of the following: i. The presence of definite joint space narrowing with sclerosis and possible deformity of bone ends ii. The presence of large osteophytes, marked narrowing of joint space, severe sclerosis and definite deformity of the proximal tibia or distal femur"

The medical record submitted with the prior authorization request satisfies each of these elements:

1. Diagnosis (Criterion A): I have a diagnosis of degenerative osteoarthritis of the knee, documented by my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, following 14 months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest.

2. Documentation of unsuccessful conservative therapy (Criterion F.1.a): I completed 18 visits of supervised physical therapy over 14 weeks (2026-04-28 through 2026-08-04), focused on quadriceps strengthening and range-of-motion work, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also completed a 4-month trial of NSAIDs with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-04 that provided only 3 weeks of partial relief. These records document a comprehensive, unsuccessful trial of non-surgical management.

3. Documentation of limited range of motion, antalgic gait, and pain on physical examination (Criterion F.1.b): My most recent examination documents varus alignment, crepitus, and effusion, with range of motion limited to 5–100 degrees. I am unable to climb stairs without assistance and wake 3–4 times nightly due to knee pain, reflecting significant functional limitation and pain on motion.

4. Radiographic evidence of severe osteoarthritis (Criterion F.1.c): Weight-bearing radiographs obtained on 2026-06-25 document bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with lateral joint-space narrowing, and a Kellgren-Lawrence grade of 4 — the most severe radiographic grade. I respectfully submit that this imaging meets the policy's description of "definite joint space narrowing with sclerosis and possible deformity of bone ends" and/or "large osteophytes, marked narrowing of joint space, severe sclerosis and definite deformity of the proximal tibia or distal femur." The denial notice does not specify which aspect of the imaging was found deficient, and I request clarification of the specific finding relied upon, as detailed below.

5. Exclusionary criteria do not apply: I am not requesting bicompartmental, customized, gender-specific, focal resurfacing, or minimally invasive knee arthroplasty. I have no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder, and my BMI is 29, which is below the policy's relative-contraindication threshold of BMI greater than 40.

Given that the submitted medical record appears to satisfy each requirement of Medical Policy BSC7.10, I ask that Blue Shield of California reverse the denial and approve the requested total knee replacement (CPT 27447).

I further request the following, consistent with my appeal rights:

- A copy of the specific clinical review notes, reviewer's rationale, and any radiology interpretation used to determine that the imaging did not support medical necessity, so that I and my surgeon may respond to the specific deficiency identified.
- Confirmation of the identity and qualifications of the reviewer(s) who made this determination, including whether the review was conducted by a physician with appropriate orthopedic expertise, as applicable under California law.
- Written confirmation of receipt of this appeal and the date by which a decision will be issued.

I understand that if this appeal is denied, I may be entitled to request an Independent Medical Review (IMR) through the California Department of Managed Health Care, and I reserve that right.

Enclosed with this letter are copies of the following records supporting this appeal:

- Physical therapy discharge summary (2026-04-28 to 2026-08-04, 18 visits)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-06-04)
- Weight-bearing knee radiograph report dated 2026-06-25
- Office examination notes documenting range of motion, gait, and functional limitations
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor, orthopedic surgery

[Enclosures list may need to be updated to match the actual documents assembled by the provider's office.]

Please contact me at [Phone Number] or [Email Address] if additional information is needed. Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Taylor Kimura
Member ID: W381271109

cc: [Dr. Okafor, Orthopedic Surgery — Office Address/Fax, if submitting jointly]

---
**Note on quoted material:** The only text above placed in quotation marks and attributed to Blue Shield of California is language retrieved directly from Medical Policy BSC7.10, "Knee Arthroplasty for Adults" (effective December 1, 2025). All discussion of how the clinical record maps to that policy is written in the patient's own words and is not itself a quotation from the plan. The denial letter did not specify which particular imaging element was considered insufficient; this letter requests that Blue Shield identify that specific deficiency so it can be directly addressed.
